reference.quote: Position of the European Parliament of 26 March 2019
decision of the Council of 15 April 2019
This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 7 June 2021.
This Directive shall apply in respect of all works and other subject matter that are protected by national law in the field of copyright on or after 7 June 2021.
reference.value: application in time: works protected on or after 2021-06-07; acts concluded and rights acquired before that date unaffected

reference.quote: Agreements for the licence or transfer of rights of authors and performers shall be subject to the transparency obligation set out in Article 19 as from 7 June 2022.
reference.value: Art. 19 transparency obligation applies to licence/transfer agreements from 2022-06-07

reference.quote: Paragraph 1 shall not apply to press publications first published before 6 June 2019.
reference.value: press publishers' right applies only to press publications first published on or after 2019-06-06 (cohort cut-off)

reference.quote: Member States shall notify the Commission of the body or mediators referred to in the first paragraph no later than 7 June 2021.
reference.value: deadline 2021-06-07 for notifying the VOD negotiation body or mediators

reference.quote: the Commission shall, by 10 April 2021, submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report on the use in the Union of the licensing mechanisms
reference.value: Commission report on extended collective licensing due 2021-04-10

reference.quote: As of 6 June 2019 the Commission, in cooperation with the Member States, shall organise stakeholder dialogues
reference.value: Commission stakeholder dialogues on Art. 17 from 2019-06-06

reference.quote: The Commission shall, by 7 June 2024, assess the impact of the specific liability regime set out in Article 17
reference.value: Commission assessment of the Art. 17(6) regime due 2024-06-07

reference.quote: No sooner than 7 June 2026, the Commission shall carry out a review of this Directive
reference.value: Commission review of the Directive no sooner than 2026-06-07

reference.quote: the services of which have been available to the public in the Union for less than three years
reference.value: service age < 3 years (jointly with turnover < EUR 10m) -> lighter OCSSP liability conditions

reference.quote: which have an annual turnover below EUR 10 million, calculated in accordance with Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC
reference.value: annual turnover < EUR 10 million (jointly with < 3 years) -> lighter OCSSP liability conditions

reference.quote: Where the average number of monthly unique visitors of such service providers exceeds 5 million, calculated on the basis of the previous calendar year
reference.value: average monthly unique visitors > 5 million (previous calendar year) -> new small OCSSPs must also make best efforts to prevent re-uploads

reference.quote: The rights provided for in paragraph 1 shall expire two years after the press publication is published. That term shall be calculated from 1 January of the year following the date on which that press publication is published.
reference.value: press publishers' right lasts 2 years, counted from 1 January of the year after publication (benefit_duration)

thresholds.note: 2-year term of press publishers' right; benefit_duration apt
Art. 22(2) only allows Member States to limit revocation to a 'specific time frame': an optional, unquantified time limit, not a numeric cutoff of this instrument (time limits are events)
Art. 8(5) only allows Member States to set 'specific requirements, such as a cut-off date': optional and unquantified, not a threshold stated in this instrument

events.note: cohort cut-off for the press publishers' right
'No sooner than' date coded as deadline; applies_to states it is the earliest date, acceptable
Expiry computed as 2021-05-17 from the Directive's OJ publication; the term runs per press publication, two years from 1 January of the year after that publication's own date

thresholds.note: trigger benefit_duration rather than eligibility; defensible since the lighter regime lasts while the service is under three years old
Art. 8(5) optional Member-State 'cut-off date': not a threshold stated in this instrument
Art. 22(2) optional Member-State revocation 'time frame': not a numeric cutoff of this instrument

events.note: 'of 17 April 2019' in the title is the same act as the signature recorded in event 3 (signed, 2019-04-17); the Council's adoption is event 2 (2019-04-15)
cohort cut-off for the press publishers' right
transposition and Art. 13 notification combined in one row (same date), acceptable
'No sooner than' date coded as deadline; acceptable
Expiry computed as 2021-05-17 from the Directive's OJ publication; the term runs per press publication from 1 January of the following year

X.note: ip_training_data primary is right. online_safety_content is a weak fit for the Art. 17 copyright liability regime, and platforms_competition (Art. 15 press publishers' right against information society service providers, Art. 17 obligations on platforms) is missing.

Y.note: ip_training_data (primary) and platforms_competition cover the operative titles.

notes: Long text (151K); reference restricted to the operative articles, header, signature block and footnotes (recitals not scanned). Reference item 17 (2-year term) is matched by the threshold rows (X thr 3, Y thr 4); both versions also code it as an expiry event with a wrong computed date. Y event 9 matches both reference items 5 (transposition) and 9 (Art. 13 notification). X adds two correct items outside the reference (Art. 19 annual reporting, Art. 10(1) six-month publicity).
